hero.headline: Turning wastewater into *materials* worth keeping.
hero.name: Shagbaor Hycent Amool
affiliations: Environmental Engineering, University of Northern British Columbia
hero.abstract:
I study how the microbes that clean industrial wastewater can also make something valuable. My PhD looks at recovering **curdlan**, a useful biopolymer, from **aerobic granular sludge**. Before this I designed farm machinery in Nigeria, lectured in engineering, earned an MSc with Distinction in Edinburgh, and started programmes that have reached thousands of students.

*Away from the lab:* I watch a lot of films mostly action, epic, and science fiction; read non-fiction and history, and like organising events that bring people together. I trained with a theatre troupe in Nigeria once; I still can't sing, and photography is next on my list. On a hard week the rule is simple: show up every day and do your best.
hero.abstract_fr:
J'étudie comment les microbes qui épurent les eaux usées industrielles peuvent aussi produire quelque chose de précieux. Mon doctorat porte sur la récupération du **curdlan**, un biopolymère utile, à partir de **boues granulaires aérobies**. Auparavant, j'ai conçu des machines agricoles au Nigeria, enseigné l'ingénierie, obtenu une maîtrise avec distinction à Édimbourg et lancé des programmes qui ont touché des milliers d'étudiants.

*Hors du laboratoire :* je regarde beaucoup de films, surtout action, épopée et science-fiction ; je lis des essais et de l'histoire, et j'aime organiser des événements qui rassemblent les gens. J'ai suivi une formation théâtrale auprès d'une troupe au Nigeria ; je ne sais toujours pas chanter, et la photographie est la prochaine sur ma liste. Les semaines difficiles, la règle est simple : se présenter chaque jour et faire de son mieux.

sections.heading: Research
sections.subtitle: PhD, Environmental Engineering, UNBC · from September 2026
sections.lede: Wastewater treatment is usually a cost. I want to know if part of it can become a *product*.
sections.body:
Coming from a background in agricultural and environmental engineering, my "lab" had always been the open field — ploughs, plants, and the stories of farmers. Joining the Research Centre for Carbon Solutions to build an electrochemical system for wastewater treatment meant stepping a long way outside my comfort zone. I learned science from the roots up there, and it is why I now ask whether treatment plants can make something instead of only destroying it.

Aerobic granular sludge is a compact, fast-settling form of the microbial communities that treat wastewater. Those microbes wrap themselves in a sticky matrix of extracellular polymeric substances (EPS). Some of that matrix may be curdlan, a β-1,3-glucan used as a gelling agent in food and studied for medical and materials uses.

My doctoral research asks whether curdlan can be recovered from sludge grown on brewery wastewater. If it can, a treatment plant could turn a disposal problem into a material.

My academic publications and research record are available on [ORCID](https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8460-6744).

steps.text: The polymer "glue" the granules build around themselves.

steps.title: Extract, identify, measure
steps.text: Show that what's recovered really is curdlan, and how much.

steps.title: Curdlan
steps.text: A recovered biopolymer with uses in food, medicine and materials.

questions: Can curdlan be recovered from aerobic granular sludge grown on brewery wastewater?
Which extraction methods recover it, and how can we show that what is recovered really is curdlan, and how much of it there is?

items.title: Integration of advanced electrocatalytic wastewater treatment with carbon utilisation
items.authors: **Amool, S. H.**, Tan, J. Z. Y., & Andresen, J.
items.plain: Cleaning industrial wastewater and dealing with carbon are usually treated as two separate problems. items.label: Preprint · SSRN · 2026
items.title: A fractional-order reduced model for predicting long-term thermal recovery from depleted hydrocarbon reservoirs
items.authors: Mzough, O. M., Nyityo, A. I., Ijir, A., Lumun, T. C., Achimba, O., Terwase, A. I., Guusu, M. J., Barakur, C. A., Shiaondo, T. L., **Amool, S. H.**, Ikyo, B., John, I. A., & Abi, D. I.
items.plain: Oil and gas reservoirs that have stopped producing still hold heat underground. This preprint builds a simplified mathematical model of how that heat behaves over the long run, which is the kind of modelling needed before anyone can judge whether an old field is worth using for geothermal energy.

items.name: Techno-Economic Studio
items.text: Carry out a techno-economic assessment step by step, from capital and operating cost to cash flow, NPV, IRR and minimum selling price, with 30 rebuilt published case studies, presets for 197 countries and 7,768 published TEAs to benchmark against.
items.classroom: walk a class through costing a process plant and reading NPV and IRR.

items.name: EIA Studio
items.text: Learn or carry out an Environmental Impact Assessment step by step, with 51 documented case studies from 40 countries and 34 national and international legal frameworks.
items.classroom: compare how different countries' laws handle the same project.

items.name: Symbiosis Workbench
items.text: Design eco-industrial parks, compare by-product exchanges, and explore evidence-based industrial symbiosis data.
items.classroom: have teams design an eco-industrial park and trade by-products.

items.name: The SustainaTable
items.text: Explore the 17 Sustainable Development Goals as a periodic table, through an engineering and resource-recovery lens. Citable with DOI [10.5281/zenodo.22957644](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22957644).
items.classroom: open a lesson by asking students to find where their discipline fits.

items.name: Laureate Lab
items.text: Apply for a scholarship with a guide at your side: step-by-step walkthroughs for 44 global and Nigerian awards, from checking you qualify to the interview, with dated plans, official links and videos. Learn from analysed winning essays in the Essay Dojo, build a competitive CV in CV Studio, and see new openings collected automatically every morning.
items.classroom: walk a class through one scholarship guide before an application clinic.

items.name: Citadel
items.text: Academic writing, made clear: 43 short units from topic development, research questions, aims and objectives, research philosophy and methodology to literature reviews, IMRaD, referencing and publishing, with a research project builder, writing tools, a reference library and a writing desk.
items.classroom: set a level as homework before the first written assignment.

items.name: Nigeria Forest Reserves Atlas
items.text: Explore Nigeria’s forest reserves, national parks, game reserves, sanctuaries, Ramsar wetlands and biosphere reserves on one map, with official boundaries, sourced profiles of plants, animals, resources and tourism, a statistics section with downloadable charts, a visit planner and a field-report hub for NGOs. Every record shows its sources and a verification level, and the full dataset downloads as CSV or GeoJSON.
items.classroom: have each group profile the reserves in their home state and compare what the records say with recent satellite imagery.

items.name: Nigeria Water Resources Atlas
items.text: Explore Nigeria’s dams, reservoirs, rivers, lakes, waterfalls, springs and Ramsar wetlands on one map, with a river flood watch that compares modelled flow on the Niger, Benue and other rivers with what is normal for the date, pages on river basins and groundwater, statistics on water access by state with downloadable charts, a visit planner and a community field-report hub. Every record shows its sources and a verification level, and the dataset downloads as CSV or GeoJSON.
items.classroom: have each group pick a river basin, compare its water per person with the national figure, and check the flood watch during the rainy season.

sections.note: Using one of these in a course or workshop? I'd love to hear how it went: [amool@unbc.ca](mailto:amool@unbc.ca). Free to use for teaching and learning.

bios.label: Medium · 100 words
bios.text:
Shagbaor Hycent Amool is an environmental engineer and PhD student in Environmental Engineering at the University of Northern British Columbia (UNBC). His research asks whether aerobic granular sludge treating brewery wastewater can yield curdlan, a biopolymer used in food, medicine and materials.

He holds an MSc in Global Sustainability Engineering with Distinction from Heriot-Watt University, where he was a PTDF overseas scholar, and a first-class BEng in Agricultural and Environmental Engineering from the University of Agriculture Makurdi (now called Joseph Sarwuan Tarka University Makurdi). A Lecturer I at Federal Polytechnic Wannune, he founded Via Scholaris and builds free interactive tools for sustainability education.

bios.label: Long · 170 words
bios.text:
Shagbaor Hycent Amool is an environmental engineer and PhD student in Environmental Engineering at the University of Northern British Columbia (UNBC) in Prince George, Canada. His doctoral research asks whether aerobic granular sludge treating brewery wastewater can yield curdlan, a biopolymer used in food, medicine and materials, turning a treatment cost into a recoverable product.

His path runs from farm machinery and palm oil milling in Nigeria to lecturing at Federal Polytechnic Wannune, an MSc in Global Sustainability Engineering with Distinction from Heriot-Watt University as a PTDF overseas scholar, and a first-class BEng from the University of Agriculture Makurdi (now called Joseph Sarwuan Tarka University Makurdi). In 2026 he won the Delegates' Prize at the ECR Net Zero Conference (Supergen), and his circular-economy venture ERGE Platform took First Prize at the Industry-Led Innovation Sprint.

He founded Via Scholaris, a free learning library for students heading into postgraduate study, and builds open interactive tools for techno-economic analysis, environmental impact assessment, industrial symbiosis and the Sustainable Development Goals.
